video_title: Wolves' joyfulness | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Lamar Jackson as the next Minnesota Vikings quarterback
quotes.excerpt: I think Lamar Jackson has to be the next quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings.
quotes.quote: I have a trade proposal, a little out of the box. It is going to hurt one of our local teams, and it is going to hurt the team that John covers, but I think Lamar Jackson has to be the next quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' injury and the Timberwolves' improved team culture
quotes.excerpt: Not only are they surviving the Anthony Edwards injury to date, the vibe, the attitude is better.
quotes.quote: Not only are they surviving the Anthony Edwards injury to date, the vibe, the attitude, the fun level around this team is 90% better than it was a year ago, and it has been so fun for me just to watch Anthony Edwards care so much and play so hard and be so invested in his teammates and his team.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' defensive impact and growth this season
quotes.excerpt: Defensively, he is battling. He is creating turnovers. He is getting out and running.
quotes.quote: Since he has arrived here, from the moment he set foot here, it has been a positive impact every single day. The most encouraging thing for the Timberwolves right now is that Anthony Edwards is starting to find his groove in terms of aggressiveness offensively, but defensively, he is battling. He is creating turnovers. He is getting out and running. He is not fouling as much the last couple of games, and I just really think that what you are seeing is a player who understands what his team needs right now and then he is providing that.

quotes.speaker: Steve Terry
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Terry's initial reaction to the Naz Reid trade
quotes.excerpt: I woke up the morning of the Naz trade. It was the Naz trade to me.
quotes.quote: I woke up the morning of the Naz trade. It was the Naz trade to me for obvious reasons. I was like, holy, what happened? And they traded Naz, and I am like, it is a kick in the stomach. I am like, okay, well, obviously business-wise, Naz is a great dude. I was just like, and then he was ready to start. The whole thing, and I was, and then I go, what did they trade him for? And John, I think you might have been the first person I called because I am like, what the, you know, not a fan. Was not a fan.

quotes.speaker: Steve Terry
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Terry's evolving perspective on Naz Reid's maturity
quotes.excerpt: He was an unserious player, and I do not think that is debatable.
quotes.quote: He was an unserious player, and I do not think that is debatable. He was not serious. The whole father, brother, it is just a circus. And if you go back and you look at YouTube videos of him literally peeling out of the parking lot and running red lights, I mean, that is, I guess, good for business in a negative way if he moved here, but that is not what serious humans do, if we are just being honest. So that is my perception, that we got a clown show coming here, and I am just and it could not be any further from the truth.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' maturity as a leader and teammate
quotes.excerpt: It is possible to be an immature human being and a mature athlete.
quotes.quote: It is possible to be an immature human being and a mature athlete. Anthony Edwards, in terms of work ethic, being a good person in the locker room, being a good person in the organization, being coachable, has been incredibly mature. And guess what? Every once in a while, he will do something in an interview or off the court where you go, that was dumb. And I think the same thing about Anthony Edwards. He might do something goofy off the court. It does not mean he cannot be a mature basketball player.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Anthony Edwards' development to Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.excerpt: I am certainly seeing parallels with Karl-Anthony Towns.
quotes.quote: I am certainly seeing parallels with Karl-Anthony Towns. I think both players arrived in the league very young, on teams that had very little veteran leadership around them, that had changes in front office, in coaches, that had a revolving door of teammates, that had just instability and a lack of talent around them, and but because both of them were sort of the one player or the constant that stayed the same as these teams changed, you started to look at it and say, well, it must be this guy's fault or he must be the immature one.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch's coaching philosophy and team culture
quotes.excerpt: Finch has kind of embraced Anthony Edwards in terms of because personalities, the two of them could not be more different.
quotes.quote: It has been fun watching Chris Finch kind of embrace Anthony Edwards in terms of because personalities, the two of them could not be more different. And generally speaking over the years, we have seen Finch gravitate to the Kyle Andersons, the Mike Conleys, the deliberate, ultra-mature, veteran guys that maybe have a few limitations in their game at the points that he connected with them, but certainly just play smart brand of basketball. Anthony Edwards is certainly a more creative, free-flowing guy. I think that he will turn the ball over a little bit more, he will take some shots that you wonder about, but I really do believe that Anthony Edwards is the kind of point guard that Chris Finch has been waiting for his whole time here in terms of the style of play, in terms of the way they want to just play basketball.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Naz Reid's recent performance and injury struggles
quotes.excerpt: He finally had a really good game, 25 points, 13 rebounds, but yeah, it has been ugly early.
quotes.quote: He finally had a really good game, 25 points, 13 rebounds, but yeah, it has been ugly early with the whole team now. They have had a ton of injuries, Rudy Gobert has been hurt, Naz Reid has been hurt, so they are short-handed going in, but I think it has been some real growing pains with Naz. There was a point where he was benched for the second half of a game because of some disagreements with Charles Lee, and it has been a rocky introduction.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' roster transition and future outlook
quotes.excerpt: The Timberwolves now are clearly in a period of transition.
quotes.quote: The Timberwolves now are clearly in a period of transition, and they decided that Anthony Edwards was not going to be a part of the team that they believe can eventually get to real contender status. They made a decision with that core group that they were not good enough as constructed and so they had to take a step back, amass some assets and go forward. And what that also means is that, A, the fans are going to be upset because they finally had a fun season last year and now it is going sideways again, but B, the possibilities of Anthony Edwards getting traded again are very high.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The JJ McCarthy trade and team management strategy
quotes.excerpt: You do not like the way things are going, you tank, and then you can be traded.
quotes.quote: You do not like the way things are going, you tank, and then you can be traded for a fifth-round draft pick. Now, the end result of that draft pick should be a second-round draft pick. Wolves will trade a second-round draft pick at JJ McCarthy back and then go win the four titles or something.

quotes.speaker: Steve Terry
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Terry's perspective on team management and coaching
quotes.excerpt: I think that certain Timberwolves players should have their replay voting rights revoked.
quotes.quote: I think that certain Timberwolves players should have their replay voting rights revoked. Like, what the, you know, some of these guys are so adamant, and we are looking at the screen, and I am like, what are we, this is not even close. And I do not know the dude's name, I am sure you know, but he sits behind coach and he is on the video the whole time, and his whole, yeah, what's his name? Jeff Newton. Okay, so Jeff, listen, bro, stop it, okay? Look at your own eyes and then tell coach, because they get sucked into this, and then it is like we lose, we are losing all our timeouts, and I am just like, what the hell are we doing? These aren't even close.

quotes.speaker: Steve Terry
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of team leadership and coaching changes
quotes.excerpt: I think it starts from the top and works its way down.
quotes.quote: I think it starts from the top and works its way down. I have sat through Rambis and just, you know, just the most ridiculous of coaches and GMs, and you know, GM clipping his toenails during tryouts. I mean, it just don't even get me started with just the crazy I've seen in my life. But the fact that you have the head coach who doesn't really, outwardly, you know, except for the Kyle Andersons and the Mike Conleys, loves him, just says he's a joy, he's just, you know, and they are giddy, and that's what, you know, when Jim was earlier just saying this is a fun team to watch.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' roster depth and player development
quotes.excerpt: The depth of talent in this league is insane right now.
quotes.quote: The depth of talent in this league is insane right now. And I do think right now it is Anthony Edwards, Jaden McDaniels, Naz Reid at the top, but yeah, like, I mean, Jaden McDaniels is coming, Naz Reid will come back, like, there is so many great players. It is just unbelievable, but yeah, like I I mean, it is incredible what Oklahoma City continues to do even with all of these guys out. They just keep winning and Anthony Edwards is the guy that just stirs that drink.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' roster management and player injuries
quotes.excerpt: They have had a ton of injuries, Kobe White has been hurt, so they are short-handed.
quotes.quote: They have had a ton of injuries, Kobe White has been hurt, so they are short-handed going in, but I think it has been some real growing pains with Anthony Edwards. There was a point where he was benched for the second half of a game because of some disagreements with Charles Lee, and it has been a rocky introduction.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' adjustment to his new role
quotes.excerpt: I think he will be fine. I think it will all work out in the long run.
quotes.quote: I think he will be fine. I think it will all work out in the long run, but, um, yeah, this this has been a real tough introduction for the Hornets in general and for Anthony Edwards in particular to a new role, to a new team, and he is just walking in footsteps that were created by Jaden McDaniels and it is it has been hard on him, I think.

quotes.speaker: Steve Terry
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Terry's perspective on team management and player trades
quotes.excerpt: Even if he was never traded, he was going to become a starter.
quotes.quote: Even if he was never traded, he was going to become a starter. That is a big change to be six-man to go to a starter, and to then get traded after you get that promotion, we will call it. And if you ever follow any of the Hornets feed, they are pissed. I mean, they are like, who is this guy? Like, you know, they do not understand the value that he brings. So not only is it does he not have that Minnesota love surrounding him anymore, which you cannot recreate, like there is never going to be towels in Charlotte. It just that is a one-time, you know, no one is getting tattoos in Charlotte. It just we have to, you know, to know that.

quotes.speaker: Steve Terry
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of team leadership and coaching on player performance
quotes.excerpt: The fact that you have the head coach who doesn't really, outwardly, loves him.
quotes.quote: The fact that you have the head coach who doesn't really, outwardly, you know, except for the Kyle Andersons and the Mike Conleys, loves him, just says he's a joy, he's just, you know, and they are giddy, and that's what, you know, when Jim was earlier just saying this is a fun team to watch. This is not the Jimmy Butler when we made the playoffs and it sucked, worst year ever. This is not Julius Randle who, you know, I personally, I think like him maybe more than most, you know, now that he's gone everyone jumps on him, but I mean, you know, he brought something to the team, but you know what he didn't bring was joy on the court.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: The potential departure of a key Timberwolves player
quotes.excerpt: I would be surprised if she comes back at this point, Jim.
quotes.quote: I would be surprised if she comes back at this point, Jim. You heard Cheryl Reeve's comments at the end of the season, and it all of it seems to be laying the groundwork for Nafisa's exit. Now, thank the Lord for the Lynx that they have Olivia Miles still here, um, to kind of rebuild around, and and and I think that her presence alone should have everyone believing that if Nafisa leaves, they will still be okay.

quotes.speaker: Steve Terry
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' roster management and team culture
quotes.excerpt: I would make the case that Finch before the season was talking about he wanted a more mature team.
quotes.quote: I would make the case that Finch before the season was talking about he wanted a more mature team, and that it was time, I think he might have said take off the diapers for, you know, the Ants and the Jadens, you know, they've been here six, seven years. And you know, I've heard this before. I would make the case that it actually has happened. This is a much more serious Timberwolves team. You look at teams last year who they lost to, and you add up those losses, it's the biggest difference between being home in the playoffs and starting on the road. It ended up not mattering, but it just this is a much more serious team.
